newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Cydsa up on sell-off rumors.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Cydsa up on sell-off rumors.

text.p: Mexican chemical company Cydsa SA (Cydsasa) was up sharply in midday trade on the Mexican Bolsa on rumors shareholder Vitro SA plans to sell its stake in the firm, dealers said.
Cydsa's benchmark A shares were up 10.24 percent to 23.15 pesos by midday. The Mexican Bolsa suspended trading on the firm earlier in the morning but had since lifted curbs, dealers said.

"It appears Vitro is restructuring and the rumors are that it will sell its stake in Cydsasa," said one dealer, who wished to remain anonymous. Two other dealers said they had also heard the same rumor.
Neither company was available for comment.

Vitro, a glass company based in Monterrey, holds a 49.5 percent stake in Cydsa, which produces chemicals and textiles mostly for export. Traders said they did not know if Vitro would sell all or only part of its stake in the firm.
Dealers said possible buyers included holding company Grupo Carso and industrial firm Alfa SA.
"People can't get enough of the Cydsa stock right now. Some say the selling price will be 30 pesos," another dealer said.
"And anything that Slim touches seems to be gold," he added.
Billionaire Carlos Slim is the controlling owner of Carso and Mexican telephone company Telfonos de Mxico.
Vitro ran into financial trouble following its purchase a few years ago of the troubled U.S.-based Anchor Glass Corp, which Vitro recently sold to Ball Foster Glass Container Co.
Vitro officials have said they wanted to sell any part of the company that did not meet strict profitability criteria.
